title: Microsoft 365 Apps cloud update: up to 10 rollout waves with custom delays for Monthly Enterprise
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout limits, licensing, defaults and controls match Microsoft's documentation. The wave overview path is supported by the configuration and monitoring pages together, and the roadmap status and dates are correctly distinguished from Learn's gradual rollout notice.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Cloud update in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center stages Monthly Enterprise updates through rollout waves.
claims.quote: Use rollout waves and update deadlines in cloud update to control when eligible devices receive updates for Microsoft 365 Apps and when users must complete installation. Rollout waves define the deployment order for devices.

claims.claim: Administrators can create up to nine custom waves using Microsoft Entra groups.
claims.quote: Create up to nine custom waves by assigning Microsoft Entra groups, for a maximum of 10 waves.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The maximum total number of waves is 10.
claims.quote: Create up to nine custom waves by assigning Microsoft Entra groups, for a maximum of 10 waves.

claims.claim: Custom delays between waves can be up to seven days per wave.

claims.claim: Devices scheduled for a channel change now follow their assigned wave.
claims.quote: Channel change now honors rollout waves, so that devices scheduled for channel change follow their assigned wave.

claims.claim: A final wave is included by default.
claims.quote: A final wave is included by default and contains all remaining devices in the Monthly Enterprise profile that aren't assigned to an earlier wave.

claims.claim: The final wave contains all remaining Monthly Enterprise profile devices not assigned to an earlier wave.
claims.quote: A final wave is included by default and contains all remaining devices in the Monthly Enterprise profile that aren't assigned to an earlier wave.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Rollout waves are optional for the Monthly Enterprise profile.
claims.quote: Rollout waves are optional for the Monthly Enterprise profile and disabled by default.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Rollout waves are disabled by default and require administrator configuration, corresponding to admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: Rollout waves are optional for the Monthly Enterprise profile and disabled by default.

claims.claim: Without waves, Monthly Enterprise devices receive updates over four to five days under the internal throttle.
claims.quote: When rollout waves aren't enabled, devices managed by the Monthly Enterprise profile receive updates over four to five days in coordination with the internal cloud update throttle.

claims.claim: Rollout waves are supported on Monthly Enterprise, not the Current profile.
claims.quote: The Current profile doesn't support rollout waves because Current Channel updates are released more frequently.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Monthly Enterprise wave delays plus the update deadline cannot exceed 25 days.
claims.quote: For the Monthly Enterprise profile, the combined total for rollout wave delays and the update deadline can't exceed 25 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft says the limit helps devices complete the update cycle within 28 days of release.
claims.quote: The total rollout wave delay and update deadline can't exceed 25 days. This limit helps devices complete the update cycle within 28 days of release.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The update applies a one-time deadline reduction where existing settings exceed the 25-day limit.
claims.quote: If your current settings exceed the 25-day limit, a one-time reduction to the update deadline will be applied with this update to meeting the new requirement.

claims.claim: All other existing rollout wave settings are preserved.
claims.quote: All other existing rollout wave settings are preserved.

claims.quote:
Enhanced rollout waves
Note
Rolling out June 2026 - July 2026.

claims.claim: Learn describes gradual rollout and warns that the experience might not yet be available in a tenant.
claims.quote: Enhanced rollout waves is rolling out gradually and might not be available in your tenant right away.

claims.claim: Group assignment for waves is separate from profile assignment.
claims.quote: Group assignment for rollout waves is separate from profile assignment.

claims.claim: The rollout wave schedule starts with each new update release.
claims.quote: The rollout wave schedule starts with each new update release, typically on Patch Tuesday.

claims.claim: Waves scheduled during a pause have already passed when the profile resumes.
claims.quote: For example, if you pause a profile on Patch Tuesday and resume it 10 days later, all waves scheduled during that period have already passed.

claims.claim: Devices still needing the update can begin receiving it when the profile resumes.
claims.quote: Devices that still need the update can start receiving it when the profile resumes.

claims.quote: Rollout waves don't apply to rollback.

claims.quote: Devices assigned later in the month are more likely to update outside the rollout wave schedule.

claims.quote: In some cases, a device in a later wave can show a completed status before its scheduled wave starts.

claims.claim: An online repair can account for completion before a device's scheduled wave.
claims.quote: This status can occur when the device is already up to date when it onboards to cloud update, when an online repair updates the installation, or when the Office Deployment Tool changes the installation and triggers an update.
